title: Dualizing complex of the point
statement:
Use the Poincare duality conventions [def-pod-conventions], with $s=\operatorname{Spec}k$, $a_s=\operatorname{id}_s$, and $\Lambda\in\{A_{E,n},\mathcal O_E,E,\Qlb\}$. On the bounded constructible point category $D^b_c(s,\Lambda)$ of [def-weil-finite-coefficient-point], the constructible exceptional inverse image [def-weil-exceptional-inverse-image] of the identity is naturally isomorphic to the identity. In particular,
$$
\omega_{s,\Lambda}=Ra_s^!\Lambda_s\cong\Lambda_s.
$$
For every $C\in D^b_c(s,\Lambda)$ put $c=\operatorname{Fib}_s(C)$, using the point fibre equivalence [lem-weil-point-fibre-equivalence], and define $D_sC=R\mathcal Hom_s(C,\omega_{s,\Lambda})$ using [def-weil-derived-pullback-tensor-hom]. Then there is a canonical isomorphism
$$
\operatorname{Fib}_s(D_sC)\cong R\operatorname{Hom}_\Lambda(c,\Lambda)=c^\vee.
$$
Here $c^\vee$ is the derived coefficient-module dual of [def-pod-perfect-point-complex]. At finite and integral coefficients the evaluation on the left means termwise sections $\Gamma(s,-)$ on the ambient derived category, as in [lem-weil-point-proetale-sections-exact]; at $E$ it means its rationalization, and at $\Qlb$ it means its common finite-stage version. Thus this formula spells out $D_sC\cong C^\vee$ under the point-category identifications, rather than identifying a sheaf complex with a coefficient-module complex without evaluation.

proof.text: Use [lem-pod-identity-compact-support-normalization] to identify $Ra_{s!}$ with the identity. The constructible adjunction in [def-weil-exceptional-inverse-image] then gives natural bijections $\Phi_K:\operatorname{Hom}(K,Ra_s^!L)\cong\operatorname{Hom}(K,L)$. At finite level use [thm-sf-ambient-adjoint-class] (2) at the identity compactification with dimension zero; bounded constructible objects have etale origin by [lem-sf-proetale-constructible-origin] (ii). Integrally use [prop-coef-integral-exceptional-adjoint] for the separated finite-type identity. For fields use [lem-sf-constructible-exceptional-adjunction-coefficients], where finite-Tor equals bounded constructible. Set $u=\Phi_{Ra_s^!L}(1)$ and $v=\Phi_L^{-1}(1)$. Naturality gives $uv=1$ and $\Phi_{Ra_s^!L}(vu)=\Phi_{Ra_s^!L}(1)$, hence $vu=1$. Naturality in $L$ gives $Ra_s^!\cong\mathrm{id}$, in particular $\omega_{s,\Lambda}\cong\Lambda_s$.

source.place: first sentence: identity compact support and uniqueness of its constructible right adjoint

proof.text: For $(R,B)=(A_{E,n},(A_{E,n})_s)$ or $(\mathcal O_E,\widehat{\mathcal O}_{E,s})$, [lem-pod-point-exact-extension-sections] gives exact $L_R\dashv\Gamma_s$ and $\Gamma_sB=R$. For $C\in D^b_c(s,R)$ its fibre $c=\Gamma_sC$ has bounded finite/finitely generated cohomology [def-weil-finite-coefficient-point]. Thus [lem-pod-point-sections-reconstruction] gives the actual isomorphism $L_Rc\to C$ and, integrally, a bounded finite-projective model $P$ of $c$.

source.place: second sentence, with its point-category identification made explicit

proof.text: Choose a flat-term K-flat representative of $c$ [lem-pc-kflat-resolution] and a K-injective resolution of $B$ [prop-pur-kinjective-resolutions-exist]. The isomorphism of Hom complexes in [lem-pod-point-derived-hom-evaluation], applied to $C\cong L_Rc$, gives $\Gamma_sR\mathcal Hom_B(C,B)\cong R\operatorname{Hom}_R(c,R)$. Its K-injective target and signed differential apply to arbitrary $c$, so finite-level perfectness is unnecessary. Integrally [lem-pod-point-completed-evaluation] identifies this internal Hom with $L_R(\operatorname{Hom}_R^\bullet(P,R))$ and puts it in $D^b_c(s,R)$. Combined with step 1 this is the finite and integral duality formula.

source.place: Tag 0A94, lemma-RHom-into-K-injective, and the Hom-complex definition; adjunction identifies every term and differential

proof.text: Apply [lem-pod-point-hom-rational-descent] to the integral comparison and the constructible finite-projective Hom model of step 3. Its rational arrow gives the formula at $E$, naturally for all localized morphisms; its specified scalar squares give the formula at $\Qlb$, independent of the common field and its morphism representatives. Finally $c^\vee=R\operatorname{Hom}_\Lambda(c,\Lambda)$ by [def-pod-perfect-point-complex], giving precisely the claimed evaluated identification.
